safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce from 3.0 to 1.5 days — explicit safety stock buffer makes SAP safety lead time redundant

narrative: Material PL1__M02238AC exhibits smooth, high-volume demand averaging 1,913 units per working day with an upward trend across the observation period and a CV of 0.24 indicating low relative variability. Lead times are bimodal and volatile (CV=0.70), alternating between rapid ~0.85-day deliveries and slower ~2.9-day batch replenishments, creating meaningful demand-during-lead-time uncertainty. The (r,Q) policy is selected: a reorder point of 7,852 units captures mean demand during lead time plus a 2,781-unit safety buffer sized to the 95th percentile of lead-time demand variability. The EOQ of 6,089 units far exceeds the MOQ of 433, reducing annual orders from ~1,104 to ~79 and cutting total inventory cost by over 90%.
warnings: SAP safety stock is 0 — no buffer against lead-time variability; stockout risk is high under current policy.
Demand outliers detected on approximately 10 days (likely plant shutdowns); winsorisation applied at 2.5th–97.5th percentile bounds.
Lead time is bimodal/volatile (CV=0.70); safety stock is sized conservatively using the combined variance formula.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) — continuous-review reorder-point with fixed Economic Order Quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth, near-normal, high-volume daily demand (CV=0.24, 100% non-zero days) with volatile lead times (CV=0.70) is the textbook case for a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. The reorder point absorbs lead-time demand uncertainty; the EOQ minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs. No intermittency, lumpiness, or structural seasonality was detected that would justify more complex policies.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding: safety_stock (2,781) + order_quantity (6,089) = 8,870 units, which is below max_storage_units (11,900). No capacity-driven service degradation expected.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (433) is well below EOQ (6,089); no MOQ-capacity infeasibility conflict.
